title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 62
paragraphs: Now Ariston, it seems, was continually stung by desire for this woman, and so contrived as follows. He made an agreement with his comrade, whose wife this woman was, that he would give him as a gift any one thing he chose from his own possessions; and he asked his comrade to make him a like return. The comrade, fearing nothing for his wife, since he saw that Ariston too had a wife, agreed; and on these terms they imposed oaths on one another. After this, Ariston on his side gave that which Agetus had chosen from Ariston's treasures, whatever the thing was; then he himself, seeking to obtain the like return, tried to take away his comrade's wife. The comrade said that he consented to give anything else except this one thing only; but at last, compelled by the oath and by the treacherous deception, he allowed her to be taken from him.
